To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phenomic traits that are important for predicting soybean yield are not always consistent with those important for predicting yield in other crops, and that these important traits are not always consistent across environments.

the combination of machine learning and optimization techniques can be used to identify a set of optimal phenomic traits to predict seed yield and that these traits are consistent across different environments.

the use of ML and optimization techniques allows for the selection of a subset phenotypic traits that will allow breeders to decrease the dependence of phenotyping on resource intensive end of season phenotyping (seed yield harvest).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of optimized phenomic predictors for efficient plant breeding decisions.
optimizing the operational efficiencies of plant breeding pipelines using ML and optimization techniques.
the development of optimized phenomic predictors for efficient plant breeding decisions using phenomic assisted selection in soybean.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phenomic traits identified in this study can be used to predict yield in the field and that these traits are useful for selecting genotypes with higher yield potential.
the results presented here provide a novel and effective approach that can be used by breeders to make informed breeding decisions in the absence of seed yield data.
phenomic data is a rich resource that can be mined to develop predictive tools that can be used to make informed decisions for plant breeding programs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrate that phenomic assisted selection is possible and that the ML algorithm, random forest, is a suitable method for phenomic trait prediction.

phenomic data can be used as a proxy for end season yield and the use of ML algorithms and optimization techniques will allow breeding programs the ability to optimize the operational efficiency of their breeding pipelines.

we have developed a phenomic predictor that can be deployed in a breeding program to make decisions about which lines to keep in the breeding pipeline and which ones to discard, and that the predictor was developed using data collected with a low-cost, high throughput phenomic sensor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phenomic data can be used to predict seed yield and the best performing ML algorithm is random forest.
phenomic data collected at any stage of crop development can be used for seed yield prediction.
phenomics can be a powerful tool to improve breeding efficiency and that the use of ML and optimization techniques can help identify optimal phenomics sensors to achieve breeding objectives.
